Important Budget Decision

A fully operational AI platform cannot run indefinitely at zero cost. AI responses, speech recognition, text-to-speech, file storage, and secure code execution all create ongoing costs.

For the initial version, which approach do you want?

A. Polished prototype — recommended for now

  • Complete animated website and dashboard

  • Functional interface and user flows

  • Simulated AI responses where necessary

  • Browser-based code execution for supported languages

  • No paid infrastructure required during design development

  • Real AI providers can be connected later

B. Free-tier functional application

  • Connect services that offer limited free usage

  • Users may encounter strict limits or temporary unavailability

  • Provider availability and limits may change

  • Suitable for testing, but not dependable for a public launch

C. Users provide their own API keys

  • The platform itself can remain inexpensive

  • Users connect their own AI-provider accounts

  • Less convenient for students and nontechnical users

  • API keys must be encrypted and handled securely

D. Local AI models

  • No per-message API charges

  • Requires a sufficiently powerful computer or server

  • Performance depends on the available hardware

  • Hosting it publicly will still cost money

Is It Ready to Use?

It is ready to use as an interactive visual prototype, but it is not yet ready as a real AI coding platform.

What Works Now

The current website can be opened and demonstrated. It includes:

  • Responsive cinematic landing-page sections and navigation.

  • A coding-assistant workspace with Learn and Solve modes.

  • A functional chat interface that displays scripted demonstration answers.

  • File-selection and attachment-preview interactions.

  • Simulated voice input and voice-tutor demonstrations.

  • Student-learning, multi-language, GitHub, live-workspace, and project-context presentations.

  • No login or account requirement, as requested. The interface explicitly presents itself as a free prototype.

You can preview it locally with:

Bash
python3 -m http.server 4173

Then open:

http://localhost:4173

What Is Not Real Yet

The application currently has no AI model or backend.

Specifically:

  • Chat answers come from three predefined JavaScript strings—not from an AI service.

  • Selecting files only displays their names; the files are not analyzed.

  • Voice input is simulated by inserting a predefined question after a timer.

  • GitHub connectivity is only a placeholder and explicitly reports that a backend is required.

  • There is no secure code execution, terminal, repository analysis, persistent conversation history, database, storage, or deployment configuration.

  • The source tree contains no backend or application build configuration.

How to Use the Current Prototype

1. Start the Website

Open a terminal and move into the project directory:

Bash
cd /workspace/desktop-tutorial

Start a local web server:

Bash
python3 -m http.server 4173

Keep that terminal open. Then open this address in your browser:

http://localhost:4173

To stop the server later, return to the terminal and press:

Ctrl+C

Opening index.html directly may work, but using the local server is more reliable.

2. Navigate the Website

The navigation bar contains links to:

  • Workspace

  • For students

  • Features

  • About

The Open workspace button jumps directly to the coding-assistant interface.

Scroll through the page to experience the cinematic transitions and animated feature sections.

3. Use the Coding Chat

Inside the workspace, you can either:

  • Type a question into the message box and press the up-arrow Send button.

  • Select one of the example prompts:

    • Explain code

    • Find a bug

    • Teach me.

Example questions include:

Explain this JavaScript function step by step
Help me find the bug in my Python code
Teach me how binary search works

The current version returns scripted demonstration responses based on the type of question.

4. Switch Between Learn and Solve

At the top of the workspace, choose:

  • Learn — intended for explanations, hints, and guided teaching.

  • Solve — intended for more direct solutions.

Clicking either option changes the active mode and shows a confirmation message.

At present, this mode switch changes the interface state but does not connect to a real AI model.

5. Select Code or Project Files

Click the plus button below the message box and choose one or more files from your computer. The interface accepts multiple file selections and displays the selected filename or number of files.

You can remove the selected attachment with the × button.

Important: the prototype currently displays the file selection but does not read or analyze the file contents.

6. Try Voice Input

Click the waveform-style microphone button next to the Send button. The interface will:

  1. Enter a simulated listening state.

  2. Display a listening notification.

  3. Insert an example voice prompt into the message box.

This demonstrates the planned voice workflow. It does not currently access your microphone or perform real speech recognition.

You can also scroll to the voice section and select Hear the experience to play the visual voice-assistant demonstration.

7. Start a New Conversation

Click New thread in the workspace sidebar. This clears the current demonstration messages and returns the interface to its welcome state.

8. View the Cinematic Story Modal

Click Watch the story in the main hero section. This opens the prototype film modal.

Close it by:

  • Clicking the × button.

  • Clicking outside the modal.

9. GitHub Button

The small repository button beside the upload control represents the future GitHub integration.

Currently, clicking it displays a message explaining that repository connections require a backend.

Current Limitation

The website is presently for previewing and demonstrating the product design. It does not yet provide:

  • Real AI-generated answers

  • Real voice recognition

  • Real text-to-speech

  • File-content analysis

  • GitHub repository access

  • Code execution

  • Live terminal access

  • Persistent conversations

Therefore, you can explore all the interface interactions, but you cannot yet use it to solve actual programming problems.

Why the Terminal Said “Nothing Was Found”

The path:

Bash
/workspace/desktop-tutorial

exists inside my development environment. It probably does not exist on your computer. You must open the terminal in the folder where you downloaded the project.

The website itself is a static site: index.html loads styles.css and app.js.

Easiest Method: Open It Without a Terminal

  1. Find the downloaded project folder.

  2. Open the folder.

  3. Locate index.html.

  4. Double-click index.html.

  5. It should open in Chrome, Edge, Firefox, or Safari.

If it opens correctly, you do not need a server for basic previewing.

Recommended Method: Visual Studio Code

Step 1: Open the Correct Folder

  1. Open Visual Studio Code.

  2. Select File → Open Folder.

  3. Select the folder containing:

    • index.html

    • styles.css

    • app.js

  4. Confirm that those files appear in the Explorer sidebar.

Do not manually enter /workspace/desktop-tutorial unless that directory actually exists on your computer.

Step 2: Install Live Server

  1. Open the Extensions section in VS Code.

  2. Search for Live Server.

  3. Install the extension published by Ritwick Dey.

  4. Right-click index.html.

  5. Select Open with Live Server.

Your browser should open an address similar to:

http://127.0.0.1:5500/index.html

This is usually the simplest solution.

Run It Using Python

Windows

First, open the project folder in File Explorer.

Click the address bar, type:

cmd

Press Enter. A Command Prompt should open inside the correct folder.

Check that the website files are present:

bat
dir

You should see:

index.html
styles.css
app.js

Then try:

bat
py -m http.server 4173

If py does not work, try:

bat
python -m http.server 4173

Open this address in your browser:

http://localhost:4173

If Windows Says Python Is Not Found

Either install Python from python.org or use the VS Code Live Server method above.

Common Errors

“The system cannot find the path specified”

You are using the wrong folder path.

Instead of copying:

Bash
cd /workspace/desktop-tutorial

open the terminal from the folder containing index.html, or use the correct local path.

For example, on Windows:

bat
cd "%USERPROFILE%\Downloads\desktop-tutorial"

On macOS or Linux:

Bash
cd ~/Downloads/desktop-tutorial

“python is not recognized” or “command not found”

Python is not installed or its command has a different name.

Try:

Bash
python3 -m http.server 4173

On Windows, try:

bat
py -m http.server 4173

If neither works, use VS Code Live Server.

“Address already in use”

Port 4173 is already being used. Start the website on another port:

Bash
python3 -m http.server 8080

Then open:

http://localhost:8080

Browser Shows a File List

You started the server from the wrong directory.

Stop the server with Ctrl+C, enter the directory containing index.html, and start it again.

Page Has No Styling

Ensure all three files are in the same directory:

desktop-tutorial/
├── index.html
├── styles.css
└── app.js

The HTML expects styles.css and app.js beside it.

Blank Page or Old Website

Try a hard refresh:

  • Windows/Linux: Ctrl+Shift+R
